ia_mother_wall.blurb: Mother Wall is the tallest face at Indian Bluffs in east-central Iowa, stretching about 75 metres along the valley. It holds 15 bolted sport lines, with most of the weight in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, one easier 5.7 and 5.9 at the low end, and a single 5.12 at the top. Expect steeper, sustained pulling rather than a beginner crag. A few unbolted chimney lines and unnamed routes also exist, and loose rock is a known hazard, so wear a helmet and test holds. From the lower lot the wall sits on your left before the next wall, across the creek, with a natural arch just to its left.

ia_east_side.blurb: East Side is a bouldering stretch along a creekside bluff in the Ozark Wildlife Area of eastern Iowa, in the walk-in-only zone. It has 12 problems, mostly V1 to V3 with a few at V4, and a handful of hard ones near V6 and V7. The boulders on this side stay in the shade for most of the day, which suits hot weather, and the bluff continues well beyond the documented lines for anyone wanting to explore.
